title: Bodily Resurrection
definition: The doctrine of Bodily Resurrection teaches that god will raise the dead bodily, showing that redemption includes the whole person and not only the soul.
summary: Bodily Resurrection names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. God will raise the dead bodily, showing that redemption includes the whole person and not only the soul. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Bodily Resurrection because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: God will raise the dead bodily, showing that redemption includes the whole person and not only the soul. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people may despise the body, fear death wrongly, or imagine salvation as escape from creation if bodily resurrection is neglected. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor the body without worshiping it. Comfort the sick, disabled, aging, and grieving with the promise that Christ will raise and renew His people. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
